newsitem.title: GERMANY: Suspected arson attack on refugees home in Dresden.
newsitem.headline: Suspected arson attack on refugees home in Dresden.

text.p: Unknown assailants lobbed a firebomb into an asylum-seekers' home in east Germany, but none of the 100 residents was injured in the suspected racist attack, police said on Monday.
Police said attackers threw the bomb through an open window, setting fire to part of the hallway in the building, but the flames were quickly extinguished by residents.
Investigators specialising in neo-Nazi and far-right extremist crime in the eastern state of Saxony were called into the case, police said.
The asylum-seekers' home in Dresden has been the target of suspected racist attacks in the past. The last was in March when a smoke bomb was thrown through an open window causing considerable damage.
The attack was remniscent of a wave neo-Nazi and racist violence following German unification in 1990 when refugee and asylum-seekers' homes were often the target of firebombings.
